context.title: A public testimony
context.text: The narrative addresses readers in a society where slavery is defended and its victims' credibility contested. Precision is part of its intervention.

context.title: Christianity and hypocrisy
context.text: Douglass distinguishes religious profession from the practices of slaveholders. The appendix prevents criticism of one from being carelessly conflated with the other.

opening: Frederick Douglass hears a slaveholder explain why teaching him to read would make him unfit for slavery. The warning gives him a purpose. Learning opens a world his enslavers need to keep closed, while making his own captivity more painful to understand. Douglass writes about violence, calculated ignorance, and the struggle to recover authority over his body and mind with a precision that refuses the reader comfortable distance. The man whom slavery was supposed to render voiceless becomes an exacting witness against it.
